candidates.title: Strip upstream tracking stack from /app/ before local use or any deploy

pcfirg.problem: The app page loads Umami analytics, the unauditable Ansvisor remote script, and rrweb session replay whose block-list omits the script-input textarea, while README and privacy.html claim no data collection.
pcfirg.cause: Upstream monetization/growth instrumentation accreted after the privacy docs were written; the fork inherits the author's keys and endpoints wholesale.
pcfirg.fix: Delete app/index.html lines 65-71 (and optionally 56-62 external fonts) in the fork; app functions fully without them.
pcfirg.impact: Fork actually delivers the privacy the README promises; nothing about local usage reaches upstream's Umami/Ansvisor instances.
pcfirg.risk: Merge conflicts on future upstream pulls touching app/index.html head.
pcfirg.goal: Loading /app/ in the fork makes zero requests to reactive-analytics.up.railway.app or ansvisor-api.konsu.dev (verifiable in DevTools network tab).

age.whatItsAgeMeans: Tracker host+key were silently swapped yesterday under an SEO commit message (0a61978) — this surface changes under commit messages that do not mention it.

candidates.routeWhy: Known problem, known 10-line fix, no design questions.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: If the fork is only ever run on localhost for reading the code, the trackers fire against upstream's own analytics and harm nobody but your data trail; deleting them costs a permanent merge seam against a fast-moving upstream.
candidates.costOfDelay: Every local session leaks usage (and possibly 30%-sampled DOM recordings) to upstream's infrastructure; if the fork is ever deployed publicly, you inherit an undisclosed-session-recording privacy posture under your name.

candidates.title: Remove public CORS-proxy fallbacks from Google Doc import

pcfirg.problem: If the author's Cloudflare Worker fails, users' Google Doc contents are fetched through api.allorigins.win / corsproxy.io — arbitrary third parties see the doc ID and full document body.
pcfirg.cause: The proxies predate the self-hosted Worker (added 2026-07-15) and were left as fallbacks despite the code's own comment saying all three were down in July 2026 and may never recover.
pcfirg.fix: Delete src/gdoc.ts:54-55 so import uses only an origin-allowlisted Worker (or fails loudly).
pcfirg.impact: Document content can no longer transit an unaccountable third party.
pcfirg.risk: Doc import breaks entirely when the Worker is down instead of silently degrading.
pcfirg.goal: No request path in src/ sends user document identifiers or content to a host outside the deployer's control plus docs.google.com.

age.whatItsAgeMeans: The hardening commit consciously kept the fallbacks — a decision made and half-implemented, not an oversight nobody saw.

candidates.routeWhy: Two-line deletion; the code comment already concedes the fallbacks are dead weight.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: Docs must already be shared 'Anyone with the link' to import at all, so the marginal exposure is the doc ID (a capability URL) plus proxy operator visibility — real but bounded.
candidates.costOfDelay: Low until the Worker has an outage; then silent third-party exposure of user documents resumes. Fork-specific: on any non-allowlisted deploy domain the Worker 403s and traffic goes STRAIGHT to the public proxies.

candidates.title: README/privacy.html privacy claims contradict shipped code

pcfirg.problem: README says 'No External Services / No Data Collection' and privacy.html omits session recording, while the app ships three telemetry loaders and external font CDNs.
pcfirg.cause: Privacy copy written for the original local-only app (README last substantive touch 2026-06-29) was never revisited as instrumentation accreted from 2026-05-09 onward.
pcfirg.fix: In the fork: rewrite README privacy section and privacy.html to match actual behavior, or make them true by doing W1 first.
pcfirg.impact: Anyone evaluating the fork from its docs is no longer misled on the product's core claim.
pcfirg.goal: Every privacy claim in README.md and privacy.html is verifiable against the network behavior of a built /app/ page.

age.whatItsAgeMeans: The docs predate the tracker growth they fail to mention — classic rot where the code moved and the promise did not.

candidates.routeWhy: Ordering note: do W1 first, then this becomes a small truthful-copy edit; W1 is the fix, this is the paperwork.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: If W1 lands, the claims become mostly true and only privacy.html's Web-Speech nuance needs a line — arguably fold this into W1 rather than track separately.
candidates.costOfDelay: Nothing much locally; reputational/legal only if the fork is published with the false claims intact.

candidates.title: staging branch auto-deploys to the production gh-pages target

pcfirg.problem: deploy.yml triggers on push to main OR staging and both publish ./dist via the same gh-pages action, so pushing any branch named 'staging' in the fork silently replaces the fork's live Pages site.
pcfirg.cause: Staging deployment was enabled on day one (2025-11-22) before the site had value, and never scoped to a separate target.
pcfirg.fix: In the fork, drop 'staging' from the trigger (or disable the workflow entirely until deployment is intended).
pcfirg.impact: No accidental publish path from experimental branches.
pcfirg.risk: None; the fork does not use a staging flow.
pcfirg.goal: Only main can publish, or the workflow is disabled.

age.whatItsAgeMeans: Untouched since repo day one — the oldest live config in the repo, running with contents:write on every push to two branches, and nobody has looked at it since.

candidates.routeWhy: One-line trigger edit; cheaper to fix than to remember.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: GitHub disables workflows on forks by default until manually enabled, so the trap is armed only if the fork owner enables Actions — which they may never do.
candidates.costOfDelay: Zero until Actions are enabled on the fork; then one mislabeled branch push publishes experiments to a public URL.

candidates.title: Delete fossil scripts: update_vite_config.js and orphan test files

pcfirg.problem: Both root-level scripts fail on execution — `node test.js` exits non-zero with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (puppeteer is in neither dependency list) and `node update_vite_config.js` crashes on a hard-coded /Users/konstantin.suvorov/ path — so every audit of this fork must prove two file-writing scripts inert before trusting the tree.
pcfirg.cause: One-off dev artifacts committed Feb-May 2026; no npm script invokes them, so nothing ever surfaced the breakage.
pcfirg.goal: No script outside scripts/ and the build config remains in the repo, and `npm run build` still exits 0.

candidates.gate: npm run build exits 0 AND Test-Path returns false for update_vite_config.js, test.js, test-history.js
candidates.pcfirgVerdict: Justified but marginal: the header shows real friction (auditor time, a broken test entry point) yet no user-visible defect. Impact and Risk are dropped as adding nothing, per the contract's merge-away rule. Batch overhead exceeds the work — fold into the W1-W4 branch as a fifth commit rather than spawning its own session.
candidates.outcomeNote: Shipped 2026-08-06 — all three files deleted. The evidenceRefs above cite files that no longer exist; they are kept as the record of what was found.

age.whatItsAgeMeans: Committed once for a one-off edit and never referenced again — textbook fossil; its age proves nothing depends on it.

candidates.routeWhy: Pure deletion, zero behavior change (verified: no npm script references any of the three). Ride along with the W1-W4 branch; not worth its own batch.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: They are inert — nothing invokes them — so deleting buys tidiness, not safety; a fork trying to stay merge-clean with upstream might leave them.
candidates.costOfDelay: Nothing much; a few minutes of every future auditor's attention.

candidates.title: Fork runs entirely on upstream author's infrastructure
candidates.pcfirgVerdict: The original W6 header FAILED the contract on two counts: its Problem was conditional ('deployed anywhere else, it would…') rather than an observable defect today, and its Goal was 'write down a decision' — a document, not a checkable state, so no hard exit criterion could exist. Correctly split into an Owner decision (D1) plus one conditional batch (W6a) that exists only under one answer.

decision.question: What is this fork for?

options.a: Read-only study of the code — no work at all; W1-W4 are optional and W6 evaporates.
options.b: Private tool on a local dev machine (the stated situation) — fully satisfied by W1+W2; W6 requires NOTHING further, because localhost:5173/4173 are already in the Worker's allowlist.
options.c: Independent deployment under another domain — unlocks W6a below.

decision.note: Under (a) and (b) there is no W6 work. Only (c) produces a batch.

pcfirg.problem: W6a, conditional on decision D1=c: from any origin other than voiceprompter.app or localhost the gdoc Worker returns 403, and once W2 removes the fallbacks Doc import fails with a generic 'try again later' message that names no cause.
pcfirg.cause: Endpoint hosts and the Worker's ALLOWED_ORIGINS are hard-coded literals belonging to upstream; nothing in the fork parameterizes them.
pcfirg.fix: Deploy the fork's own copy of cloudflare/gdoc-proxy with the fork's origins in ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and point src/gdoc.ts at it.
pcfirg.impact: The fork owns every endpoint it depends on.
pcfirg.risk: Needs a Cloudflare account plus a rate-limiter binding, and the deployed Worker then inherits the manual repo-vs-dashboard sync burden the file itself warns about.
pcfirg.goal: Importing a public Google Doc from the fork's deployed origin returns its text — provable by a 200 from `curl -H 'Origin: <fork-origin>' <fork-worker>/?id=<known-public-doc>`.

age.whatItsAgeMeans: Age is structural, not temporal — the coupling has existed since the endpoints were added and deepens with each upstream commit.

candidates.routeWhy: Re-routed from just-do-it: under D1=c this is gated implementation work with a curl-shaped exit code, which is the batch definition. Under D1=a or D1=b it is not work at all. It was never a study — nothing here is unknown.
candidates.steelmanAgainst: If the fork exists only to read the code or send upstream PRs, decoupling is wasted work and permanent merge friction; and self-hosting the Worker buys a sync obligation the repo already admits it handles by hand.
candidates.costOfDelay: Zero under D1=a/b. Under D1=c it is a launch blocker, not a delay cost — Doc import is simply broken until it is done.
